description.narrative:
The objectives of the intervention did not change, but they were updated based on the New Strategic Note for UN Women 2021-2024 approved in October 2021. The main objective is "to contribute to the efforts carried out by Colombia to face the challenges and opportunities identified, mainly gender inequalities, to strengthen the empowerment of women and girls, their participation in the consolidation and stabilization in the territories and to guarantee their right to have a life free of violence".
The new structure of the Strategic Note differs from the previous one, based on the government's request to align it to the UN Cooperation Framework (UNSSCDF), but there are no substantial changes. All previous components and working lines are included in the following three areas:
1) Stabilization: Peace with Legality;
2) Migration as a development factor; and
3) Technical assistance for the acceleration of catalyst Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
Sweden's support is aligned with Areas 1 and 3 where peace issues and political and economic empowerment activities are included.

The overall objective of this unearmarked support to UN Women in Colombia is to contribute to strengthen the political and economic empowerment of women and their right to a life free from violence, both in the context of the conflict as well as beyond it, in a way that supports the construction of stable and sustainable peace. To achieve this, UN Women focuses on reaching the following results:
1) Increasing women’s leadership and participation in decision-making at all levels. 2) Economically empowering women, particularly the poorest and most excluded. 3) Guaranteeing a life free of violence for women and girls. 4) Shaping peace and security, and humanitarian action through female leadership and participation.
The support is a continuation of two previous phases with ID-numbers: 61000962 and 52060066.

UN Women:s kontor i Colombia har överlämnat ett förslag till Sveriges Ambassad i Bogotá om finansiering på 49 MSEK för att stödja implementeringen av det Landspecifika Strategiska Dokumentet i Colombia (Strategic Note Colombia) under perioden den 1 juni 2018 – 31 december 2021.
Det övergripande syftet med insatsen är att stärka den politiska och ekonomiska egenmakten av kvinnor och deras rätt till ett liv fritt från våld, både i kontexten av konflikt likväl som bortom detta, på ett sätt som stödjer byggandet av en varaktig och hållbar fred. I avsikt att uppnå detta, kommer UN Women under denna period att fokusera på följande områden: 1) Kvinnor leder och medverkar i beslutstagande på alla nivåer; 2) Kvinnor, särskilt de fattigaste och mest exkluderade, åstadkommer ekonomisk egenmakt genom och med fördel av utveckling; 3) Kvinnor och flickor lever ett liv fritt från våld; 4) Fred och säkerhet, och humanitära aktioner är formade av kvinnligt ledarskap och deltagande.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
Sida's flexible support to UN Women Colombia's Strategic Note (SN) has contributed to the triple mandate of the organization (normative, coordination and programmatic), where two areas of intervention were prioritized: 1. Women, Peace and Security (previously called "Stabilization: Peace with Legality"), and 2) Technical assistance for the acceleration of catalyst Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
Some of the results achieved throughout the implementation of the contribution are outlined below:
1. Women, Peace and Security (Stabilization: Peace with Legality)
- Since 2018, UN Women delivered targeted technical support with the aim of promoting the application of international standards in the investigation of sexual and gender-based violence to the institutions that make up Colombia's Comprehensive System of Truth, Justice, Reparation and Non-Repetition. This support has been focused on five macro-cases, as well as on different phases of macro-case 011 which investigates sexual violence in the context of armed conflict.
- Regarding the Truth Commission (CEV), UN Women contributed both financially and technically to the development of the chapter My Body is the Truth, addressing the experiences of women and LGBTIQ individuals, and its accompanying transmedia version, launched in 2022. In collaboration with Sweden and the the Truth Commission, UN Women also finalized and widely disseminated the documentary When the Waters Flow as One, which highlights the key role Colombian women have played in peacebuilding in the public agenda. As of December 2023, the film had been screened over 150 times in more than 17 countries, reaching over 15,000 in-person viewers.
- Sweden and UN Women have actively participated in the "International component for monitoring the implementation of the gender measures of the peace agreement". Alongside FDIM and the office of the Special Representative for Sexual Violence, they helped develop comprehensive progress reports produced in collaboration with the Kroc Institute documenting achievements, setbacks, and best practices. Women's participation in territorial selection processes for the Special Instance for Women has also been supported over two terms. This mechanism, created by the Peace Accord, plays a critical role in monitoring and promoting the implementation of gender commitments.
- Moreover, UN Women supported the drafting of a Roadmap for Colombia's National Action Plan (NAP) on resolution 1325. This participatory process involved more than 1,500 women who contributed through macro-regional forums, territorial meetings, and sectoral gatherings. It was conducted in collaboration with the National Government and the Promotion Committee of women's organizations, with active backing from Sweden and the International Cooperation Gender Roundtable. The plan was approved in 2025.
- Another key area of work has been the facilitation of political platforms that unify diverse women's' groups around shared peace agendas. With support from Sweden, UN Women helped sustain Women and Peace Summits (Cumbre Nacional de Mujeres por la Paz), as well as women's coalitions active in various peace processes, including negotiations with the E LN and other actors involved in the Total Peace (Paz Total) agenda.
- Another important result is that together with ProDefensoras, UN Women supported the creation of seven safe spaces and support systems providing physical safety, social support, and educational resources. They also established two shelters for Indigenous women, eight local protection and prevention routes for women human rights defenders, four emergency and rapid response funds, and published four Defenders Reports (for Chocó, Nariño, Cauca, and Antioquia) with recommendations to national and local authorities on how to address the individual and collective risks facing women defenders.
2. Technical Support to Advance SDG-Related Priorities
- Through the More Women, More Democracy (Más Mujeres, Más Democracia) initiative, carried out in partnership with Sweden, UN Women promoted the political empowerment and representation of women across electoral cycles at the territorial level in 2019 and 2023 and at the national level in 2021. While not exclusively attributable to this initiative, these efforts supported tangible progress. As a part of the initiative, 1,000 women were trained on the political system, planning tools, and rights frameworks through a 100-hour course. The National Summit of Elected Women and three departmental summits (in Cauca, Nariño and Chocó) allowed women to network, exchange experiences, and strengthen alliances for equality. Altogether, 309 women participated. The initiative also included work to advance gender equality in the private sector. This involved the creation of the WEPs Business Community (Comunidad de empresas WEPs en Colombia), which by the end of 2023 had 121 companies committed to women's economic empowerment. It supported local development efforts such as in Nariño, promoted women-led products through La Tienda de la Empatía, and helped strengthen public-private partnerships. In the field of communications, it supported the From Equal to Equal Awards, which since 2016 has recognized inclusive advertising campaigns from across Latin America.
- UN Women also contributed to key legislative achievements. It provided technical advice in shaping new gender parity rules for candidate lists and supported the passage of Law 2126 (on Family Police Stations) and Law 2114 (extending paternity leave and allowing for shared parental leave). With Swedish support, Congress conducted two rounds of the Gender-Sensitive Parliament Self-Assessment (2019 and 2024), identifying institutional improvements related to gender equality commitments.
- UN Women supported several key public policy processes in Colombia. In 2019, it provided technical assistance and inputs that led to the inclusion of a gender chapter in the National Development Plan 2018-2022 for the first time, and organized the first Summit of Elected Women, attended by the Vice President. In 2020, it supported the Congress in adopting gender parity measures in electoral lists and the legal definition of violence against women in politics.
- Efforts to improve gender-related data and planning continued at national and local levels. In coordination with the National Department of Statistics (DANE) and Presidential Advisory Office for Women's Equality, UN Women produced two editions of Colombia's National Gender Profile. The second edition, Women and Men: Gender Gaps in Colombia, served as a foundation for the National Development Plan 2022-2026. UN Women also helped develop Territorial Gender Profiles to support local authorities in integrating gender analysis into development planning.
- In 2023, work to institutionalize gender-responsive budgeting progressed. UN Women supported the expansion of the Gender Budget Tracker, enabling 360 projects in 20 territories to be marked with a gender perspective. The first Gender Budget Report was submitted to Congress, and three additional editions were supported through technical assistance.
- During the reporting period, UN Women also facilitated inclusive participation in the creation of Colombia's new national public policy on gender equality (2022-2030), formally adopted as CONPES 4080 of 2022.
- Lastly, in Bogotá, UN Women collaborated with the city's Mayors Office to strengthen the care economy. Supported by Sweden, this alliance focused on linking the care agenda with private sector engagement and launched the Bogotá in Equality Seal to mainstream gender into city governance. A reintegration pilot for women in urban settings was also carried out, innovating in how care policies intersect with peacebuilding and inclusion.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
